evidence.V1: The three-quarter view reads as a log thanks to the ringed end grain, but the front and silhouette read as a generic rounded rod or sausage and the side stub is only a tiny nub.
evidence.V2: One big tube form plus end-grain rings. The stub is a tiny small detail, there are no bark ridges, knots or split ends, and there is no medium tier.
evidence.V3: The gentle bend helps, but it is essentially an 8-sided tube of even thickness with no taper, root flare or broken end.
evidence.V4: The end cap has a soft rounded rim that catches light, but the long bark facets meet at crisp creases and the stub is unchamfered, so edges are inconsistent.
evidence.V5: Close bark and end-grain studio shots are clean: smooth gradients over the facets, no pinches or seams. The end-grain rings are flat vertex-colour bands with no z-fighting.
evidence.V6: One bark hue in 2 values plus a cream/tan end-grain secondary with dark rings. Disciplined, and the birch and redwood colourways hold.
evidence.V7: 656 tris against a medium target of 2000, so it is well under target.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material, smooth fused organic shell, bark brown plus cream end grain. Consistent with the kit.
evidence.V9: Studio line: static scenery, Anchored, Hull fidelity, CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre. Correct.

top_fixes: Add medium-scale bark detail (a few raised bark strips or grooves, a knot) and a larger branch stub so the side silhouette reads as a log
Add a taper and slight end flare, or a jagged broken end on one side, to break the rod silhouette
Bevel the long facet creases slightly so edge treatment matches the rounded end rim
